filler: Nicaragua (Estelí and Jalapa, Corojo 99 and Criollo 98 with medio tiempo)
factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: A Nicaraguan puro made entirely from Aganorsa's own farm tobacco, with a Corojo 99 wrapper and a little rare medio tiempo leaf in the filler. It was the first new line after Casa Fernandez renamed itself Aganorsa Leaf in 2018.
notes: The maker now lists it as Signature Corojo and ships it in small allotments a few times a year. Maker and Neptune rate it medium; halfwheel's review found it medium-full in strength with a full body.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: The maduro follow-up to Signature Selection, keeping the same Nicaraguan binder and filler but using a shade-grown Corojo 99 wrapper from Jalapa that is fermented dark. It is a Nicaraguan puro from Aganorsa's own farms.
notes: Also sold as Signature Selection Maduro. The maduro wrapper is Nicaraguan corojo, not broadleaf or San Andrés. The maker's page lists the Corona Gorda at 6 x 46; halfwheel and Neptune list 6 x 44. Halfwheel's review found it builds to full strength by the end.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí

Halfwheel lists the Robusto at 5 1/4 x 52.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: The San Andrés wrapped follow-up to Rare Leaf Reserve, with a double Nicaraguan binder and Aganorsa filler from Estelí and Jalapa. Like the original, it is sold only through Aganorsa Select retailers.
notes: Maker and Neptune rate it full; halfwheel's review found it closer to medium-plus strength with a medium body. Halfwheel calls the 6 x 52 a Belicoso and lists the Robusto at 5 1/4 x 52.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: A Corojo 99 dominant Nicaraguan puro from Aganorsa, known for its bright, colorful bands. It comes out in batches about twice a year, each time in a different size.
notes: Not a true limited edition, but each size ships in small batches and sells out, so what is on the shelf changes. The full blend is not published beyond being Corojo 99 dominant. The maker's strength graphic sits between medium and medium-full; Neptune lists medium.

about: Aganorsa's core Connecticut cigar, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over Aganorsa-grown Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is one of the four blends in the company's La Validación series.
notes: Formerly Casa Fernandez Aganorsa Connecticut, renamed Aganorsa Leaf Connecticut in 2018 and repackaged in 2022 as La Validación Connecticut. Aganorsa also sells a separate Aniversario Connecticut. Halfwheel lists the Toro at 6 1/4 x 52.
verifyNotes: Notes: removed the unsupported claim that the Aniversario Connecticut is pricier. Strength confirmed as 3 of 5 on the maker's graphic.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: A Nicaraguan puro created by Max Fernandez of Aganorsa and Kyle Gellis of Warped Cigars, named for the American bulldogs that guard Aganorsa's farms and factory. Each size is named after one of the dogs.
notes: Launched as a Warped and Casa Fernandez collaboration. The maduro version is sold as Guardian of the Farm NightWatch, and Cerberus is a separate Corojo 2012 wrapped blend. Halfwheel's review put the body a little above medium.

factory: Aganorsa (formerly Tabacos Valle de Jalapa S.A., TABSA), Estelí
about: The oversized, value-priced branch of Aganorsa's JFR (Just For Retailers) brand, with ring gauges running up to 80 and beyond. It started with the 8 x 80 Mambo in a San Andrés maduro wrapper.
notes: Lunatic is a family. Details here are the original Lunatic Maduro. Lunatic Habano uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over the same Nicaraguan binder and filler; Lunatic Locos and Lunatic Torch are separate corojo wrapped blends. The maker's strength graphic sits between medium and medium-full; Neptune lists the Maduro as full.

about: A value-priced Nicaraguan puro from Aganorsa's JFR (Just For Retailers) brand, with a corojo wrapper, a tucked foot and a pigtail cap. The JFR brand is known for large ring gauges.
notes: JFR stands for Just For Retailers and was built for brick-and-mortar shops. Neptune's write-up calls it full-bodied while listing its strength as medium.
verifyNotes: about: removed the claim that JFR is the company's best seller; no source opened says so.

about: The maduro version of Aganorsa's value-priced JFR (Just For Retailers) line, finished with a tucked foot and a pigtail cap. It is the stronger of the two main JFR blends.
notes: Sources disagree on the wrapper: the maker's site lists Mexican San Andrés Maduro, while halfwheel (2022) and Neptune describe a Nicaraguan puro with a fermented corojo maduro wrapper. Strength is from the maker's 4 of 5 graphic; Neptune lists medium.

factory: Tabacalera AJ Fernandez Cigars de Nicaragua S.A.
about: A box-pressed Nicaraguan puro blended by Rafael Nodal and made by AJ Fernandez in Estelí. The Maestro size was Cigar Aficionado's No. 1 Cigar of 2019 with a 96 rating.
notes: Altadis lists the wrapper as Nicaraguan Sumatra; halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado only say Nicaragua. Strength is Neptune's rating, as Altadis does not give one. Quattro Nicaragua Sonata and Concerto are separate, later blends.

about: The original box-pressed Aging Room Quattro, made by Jochy Blanco at Tabacalera Palma with an aged Sumatra wrapper grown in Indonesia over Dominican tobacco. As the Quattro F55 Concerto it was Cigar Aficionado's No. 2 cigar of 2013.
notes: Formerly called Quattro F55; renamed Quattro Original in 2018. Cigar Aficionado rates it medium-full while Neptune lists full. It is no longer on Altadis USA's Aging Room page and Neptune shows it sold out, so current availability is unclear.

about: The mildest of the box-pressed Aging Room Quattro blends, with an Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade wrapper over Dominican binder and filler. It was added to the Quattro series in 2018 and made at Tabacalera Palma.
notes: Neptune marks every size discontinued and it is no longer on Altadis USA's Aging Room page. Strength is Neptune's rating; no maker rating was found.

about: The Quattro Original blend with a Mexican San Andrés maduro wrapper in place of the Sumatra leaf. It began in 2017 as a Thompson exclusive called Quattro F55M before going national.
notes: Formerly Quattro F55M (F55 Maduro); renamed Quattro Maduro in 2018. Neptune marks every size discontinued and it is no longer on Altadis USA's Aging Room page. Strength is Neptune's rating; halfwheel's 2017 review found it medium-plus in strength with a medium body.
verifyNotes: Notes: added halfwheel's review strength, which is lower than Neptune's full rating. Sources: swapped the Thompson news item for halfwheel's review, which covers the same launch facts.

about: A Nicaraguan puro from Rafael Nodal made by the Plasencia family, using tobacco from four Nicaraguan growing regions. The name means pure bred in Spanish.

about: A Dominican puro from Rafael Nodal's core Aging Room line, made at Jochy Blanco's Tabacalera Palma. It came out of the 2018 overhaul of the Aging Room portfolio alongside Connecticut and Maduro versions.
notes: Launched as Aging Room by Rafael Nodal Habano; retailers call it Core Habano. No published strength rating was found. Neptune has no sizes in stock and it is not on Altadis USA's Aging Room page, so it may be discontinued.

about: The first regular production line from All Saints Cigars, the company co-founded by former CAO sales head Micky Pegg. It is made at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory with a San Andrés wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco.
notes: The maker calls it medium bodied; halfwheel's review found the strength below medium. Sizes are the four listed since September 2025. It launched with Berkey (5 1/2 x 50), Commandant (6 1/2 x 52), Huge and Coach (7 x 48, now discontinued). A Dedicación Habano version is a separate blend.

No All Saints line by this name could be confirmed. The maker and halfwheel list four blends: Dedicación, Dedicación Habano, St. Francis and St. Francis Colorado. The original Dedicación wears a dark Mexican San Andrés wrapper, so this is most likely that cigar.

about: The second All Saints line, named for Francis of Assisi and made at Rocky Patel's TAVICUSA factory with a dark Ecuadorian oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. The Cigar Authority named it its 2021 Cigar of the Year.
notes: The maker calls it medium-full bodied; Neptune calls it full. Sizes are the four listed since September 2025. It launched with Robusto (5 1/2 x 50), Toro (6 1/2 x 52), Huge and Churchill (7 x 48). St. Francis Colorado is a sister blend with an Ecuadorian Habano Colorado wrapper.

about: The limited edition that launched All Saints Cigars in December 2019, sold in a single 5 x 58 size. It returned in October 2023 in a run of 500 boxes of 23.
notes: Filler is as listed for the 2023 release; the 2019 original was described as all Nicaraguan under the wrapper. Neptune calls it medium strength, while halfwheel's 2023 review found mild to medium strength with a full body.
